note: KVCacheSimple.step 256 -> 512 on 0863b06. The ranked window is a 512-row seed followed by 512 decode rows, so every full-attention cache walks offset 0 -> 1024 exactly once. At step=256 that costs three allocations per cache -- 512 at the seed, then two grow-and-concat events inside the decode window (512->768 copying 512 rows, 768->1024 copying 768 rows). At step=512 the seed allocates the same 512 rows (nSteps = ceil(512/512) = 1, so the timed prefill is byte-identical and pays no unused-tail zeros -- that over-allocation is what made the step=1024 sibling bfd12563 read -0.025%) and the decode window does ONE 512->1024 concat copying 512 rows. Per cache per window: one fewer allocation, one fewer concat of K and one of V, and 768 fewer rows moved. Sixteen full-attention caches on the serial control leg, those sixteen plus the persistent head-history cache on the MTP leg. Token-neutral by construction: `step` enters `update` only through the allocated capacity. `offset` advances by the row count alone, writes stay at [previous, offset), reads are the `..<offset` views, `trim` moves only `offset`, and the grow path slices the live prefix before concatenating, so every consumer sees the same K/V rows at the same positions on both settings. Proven by simulation over the ranked call sequence for both legs, rollbacks included: identical offsets and identical returned views at every call. No kernel, no schedule, no head tensor changes. Widths 2...9, IPG table, tablePays>=4, probe fraction 0.15, skip-probesort gate and the xsums fill fusion all carried forward unchanged from 0863b06; Qwen35.swift and Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift are byte-identical to the parent.
